subject: Astronomy & Space
title: Stonehenge and the Sun
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Stonehenge and the Sun.

hook.text: Stonehenge's stones align perfectly with the sunrise on the summer solstice. It was built 5,000 years ago.

buildup.text: Ancient Britons moved 25-ton stones over 200 km to construct it. The effort suggests deep astronomical purpose.

discovery.text: The alignment tracks the Sun's extreme positions on the horizon—solstices and possibly lunar cycles too.

twist.text: Stonehenge may have been a calendar, a temple, or both. After 5,000 years, we still debate its exact purpose.

climax.text: Similar stone alignments exist worldwide—from Egypt to Peru. Ancient peoples everywhere watched the sky with precision.

punchline.text: Five thousand years old. Still aligned. The sky was humanity's first clock.

quiz.question: What astronomical event does Stonehenge align with?
options: The sunrise on the summer solstice
The position of the North Star

details.summary: Stonehenge, built in stages from about 3000 to 2000 BCE, aligns precisely with the summer solstice sunrise and winter solstice sunset. This Neolithic monument demonstrates that ancient peoples tracked celestial cycles with remarkable precision, likely for agricultural timing, ritual purposes, and…
details.whyItMatters: Stonehenge proves that astronomical observation predates writing, mathematics, and civilization itself. Humans have been studying the sky for at least 5,000 years — astronomy is arguably humanity's oldest science.
takeaways: Stonehenge aligns with summer solstice sunrise and winter solstice sunset
It was built in stages from about 3000 to 2000 BCE
It shows astronomy predates writing and mathematics

faq.question: Was Stonehenge an observatory?
faq.answer: It's debated. The solar alignments are undeniable, but whether Stonehenge served primarily as an observatory, a ceremonial site, a healing center, or a combination is uncertain. The astronomical alignments may have been one function among many for this remarkable monument.

faq.question: Are there other ancient astronomical structures?
faq.answer: Many. Newgrange in Ireland (winter solstice alignment, 3200 BCE), the Goseck Circle in Germany (solar observatory, 4900 BCE), and Nabta Playa in Egypt (stone circle with stellar alignments, 5000 BCE) all demonstrate that sky-watching was a universal human activity across cultures.
